newsitem.title: USA: Sprint ordered to rehire 177 workers.
newsitem.headline: Sprint ordered to rehire 177 workers.

text.p: The government ordered Sprint Corp. to rehire and pay full back pay and benefits to 177 workers whose San Francisco telemarketing office was shut down during a union organising drive in 1994, the Communications Workers of America said Monday.

The National Labour Relations Board, in a decision released Monday, ruled that Sprint's sudden closing of the marketing office in July 1994, just one week before a scheduled union election, violated federal law, the union said.
The office, which employed mostly Hispanic women, was called La Conexion Familiar, Spanish for "The Family Connection."
The union said the NLRB upheld an appeal by the union of a decision by an administrative law judge.
It said the board rejected Sprint's contention that it closed the office because it was losing money.
The NLRB ruling will require Sprint to rehire the workers and give them "a position in its existing operations that is substantially equivalent to the employee's former position," the union said.
Sprint must pay appropriate moving expenses and pay them compensation for wages and benefits, plus interest, from the date of the closing to the date they are rehired, it said.
The Communications Workers of America represents more than 600,000 workers in telecommunications, television, journalism and publishing and the public-service sector.
Sprint stock rose 50 cents to $40.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
